3. RATIONAL FUTURE FUNCTIONS AND FINITE GRID
Fix
  h=1/10^12, t=1/1000, tau=1/2000000.
Let
  E_h=sum_(n=0)^4 (hL)^n/n!,
  E_t=sum_(n=0)^16 (tL)^n/n!, K=E_t^T.
For k=0,...,4 let (a_k,b_k^x,b_k^y) be the first three entries of column 3+k of E_h. These are rational. At the first order,
  a_k+b_k dot x=eta h l_k(x)+O(h^2 sqrt(1+|x|^2)), eta=1/10.
More precisely the vector of five remainders has Euclidean norm <=5h^2 sqrt(1+|x|^2), because ||E_h-I-hL||_2<5h^2.

Write I0=1_{Y0=0}, psi_k=1_{Y0=0,Yh=k+1}. The two-by-two matrix B_h with rows b_4^T,b_0^T is invertible, with ||B_h^(-1)||_infinity<12/h. Define two rational bounded functions by
  (F_x,F_y)^T=B_h^(-1)(psi_4-a_4 I0, psi_0-a_0 I0)^T.
Then define the eight-component future function
  F=(I0,F_x,F_y,1_{Y0=1},...,1_{Y0=5}).
It depends only on Y0,Yh. Each coordinate F_x,F_y has absolute value <=20/h, and ||F||_2<=30/h pointwise. Put
  D_k=psi_k-a_k I0-b_k^x F_x-b_k^y F_y.
All |D_k|<=7 pointwise; D_0 and D_4 are identically zero by construction.
Put G=U_t F-KF, where U_t shifts both arguments of F by t. Then ||G||_2<=61/h pointwise.

For a future function A, write A^+ for its value on the positive half of the observed window, and A^- for the same function with time labels reversed. Thus F^- uses Y0,Y_-h and (U_tF)^- uses Y_-t,Y_(-t-h). Every statistic below depends only on the seven observed letters at
  -t-h, -t, -h, 0, h, t, t+h.
The observation span is T=2(t+h)<1/400. There are at most 6^7=279936 possible observed words. No hidden variable is supplied to the statistic.

4. OBSERVED LINEAR STATISTICS
Define
  p0=E I0,
  s2=E[F_x^- F_x^+ +F_y^- F_y^+],
  R_h=E sum_k D_k^- D_k^+,
  R_t=E sum_(ell=0)^7 G_ell^- G_ell^+.
For each i define b_i=Z_i dot (I-K)xi_i and let the rational quadratic
  q(x,y)=alpha_0+alpha_1 x+alpha_2 y+alpha_3 x^2+alpha_4 xy
be the unique solution V alpha=(b_i)_i. Its coefficients obey |alpha_j|<1/10. Hence for |y|<=1,
  |q(x)-q(y)| <= (1+|x|)|x-y|.
Its observed expectation statistic is
  S_q=E[alpha_0 I0 + (alpha_1/2)(F_x^-+F_x^+)
       +(alpha_2/2)(F_y^-+F_y^+)+alpha_3 F_x^-F_x^+
       +(alpha_4/2)(F_x^-F_y^+ +F_y^-F_x^+)].
Each displayed quantity is a linear function of the finite seven-time probability table. The definitions remain valid for arbitrary observed stationary laws; R_h,R_t need not be nonnegative outside equilibrium.
